Messages.Author: Malcolm Sprye
Messages.Body:
Okay, So I searched the old boards, and the new, and didn't really find an answer to this.

If you Malkavian Time Auction and sell off a Blood Doll, does the winner get to move it to one of his minions? I can't remember where I read it, but I'm pretty sure Vessel/BD belong to whoever controls the minion (so you could take control of someone's vampire, and use the BD on them). So that would mean that you can't Own a BD on someone else's minion.

What about Villein? Would they get to move it? Would moving it count as playing it on the new minion (and allow them to pull blood off)?

Messages.Author: the1andonlime
Messages.Body:
Not sure what the Time Auction does (card text would have been nice), but as a general rule, Master cards are controlled by the player who played them until an effect dictates a change of controller.

As for Villein, unless MTA states "as if it was played from hand" or something to that effect, it is just moved to a new minion and will affect future Villeins and Minion Taps played by the new controller.

Messages.Author: the1andonlime
Messages.Body:
> Malcolm wrote:
> I can't remember where I read it, but I'm pretty sure Vessel/BD belong to whoever controls the minion (so you could take control of someone's vampire, and use the BD on them). So that would mean that you can't Own a BD on someone else's minion.
>
BD & Vessels (like all Master cards) are controlled by the player who played them.

You can play a Vessel on someone else's vampire (card text), but he or she gets to decide whether or not to use the Vessel (also card text).

You cannot play a BD on someone else's vampire (card text), but if can use a BD played by someone else that somehow ended up on a vampire you control.

The BD and Vessel (like all other cards) leave play when the controller is ousted. For example:
- You play Vessel on your predator's vampire and get ousted. Said Vessel leaves play
- You play BD on your vampire, which subsequently gets stolen by your prey via Temptation of Greater Power, who then back-ousts you with Kindred Spirits. Said BD is leaves play but the vampire stay on the table

Always remember that:
- you control all Master cards you play
- minion cards are controlled by either the controller of the minion it is on, or the player it is currently with (for cards like Army of Rats)
- card text trumps all rules they contradict

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
Since there is no ruling, by default the master stays put, although the control changes.

According to rules section 1.6.3, a minion card is controlled by the controller of the minion it is on. Therefore, if another player takes control of a minion card that must be put on a minion (retainer, equipment, some locations), he would have to put it on a minion he controls in order to take control of it. LSJ's ruling just clarified what was already in the rulebook.

There is no rule that connects the control of a master card with the controller of the minion it is placed upon. Therefore, logically, there is no reason why a player who takes control of such a master card through MTA would get to move it. Since there is no ruling to the contrary, that is the rule. No need for "official clarification", really.

In some cases, taking control of a master card on another player's minion has little relevance, e.g., disciplines, Blood Doll. In other cases, it is substantive, like for cards that can be removed through a  action, such as Pentex.

Messages.Author: AaronC
Messages.Body:
Good research.

I have to wonder why such research is even necessary. These aren't rulings - they are what I would call "clarifications." Neither the rulebook nor the text of MTA implies that the placement of a master-on-a-minion would get moved by MTA. It is already established that a player can control a master placed on another player's minion. Ergo, logic dictates that the master-on-a-minion whose controller changes does not get moved. A "clarification"/"ruling" is nice for those who dare not read and analyse the rules themselves, but it shouldn't be necessary.

It's like everyone wants to make sure that LSJ didn't make some exception to the rules that he hid in some obscure newsgroup posting. I really don't like this "common law" approach to rules, which I guess is odd since I live in a common law country. Maybe someday we'll get a "civil code" approach.

Messages.Author: Malcolm Sprye

More to the point, the natural instinct (at least mine), is that if you buy a card, and gain control of it... it would go to your controlled region by default. You don't go to the store and pay for a gallon of milk, and then put a sticker on it that says "I own this milk"... and leave the milk.

It may turn out that's how it works, but seeing as how it's a very unusual card, I don't feel "rules lawyery" for asking for a complete ruling.
